description: Open-source, agent-agnostic daily journaling harness: user journal -> AI estimates PAD / G / XP with provenance -> daily report -> in-note feedback -> rule calibration. Read docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md first. Python 3 standard library only. Quality check: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

userStories.title: Package scaffold and config loader
userStories.description: As a user, I configure the system with one trace.toml file.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/__init__.py, etrace/__main__.py and etrace/config.py exist
config.load(path) reads TOML via tomllib: timezone (default America/Chicago), data_dir, preset (default 'default'), language ('zh' or 'en'), schedule times for calibrate/daily/g
Unknown keys raise a clear error; missing optional keys get defaults
examples/trace.toml documents every key
tests/test_config.py passes
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Append-only JSONL store with locking
userStories.description: As the engine, I need safe storage that never loses or rewrites history.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/store.py: append(name, record), read_all(name), write_json_atomic(path, obj) using temp file + os.replace
A lock file prevents two writers at once; stale locks older than a configurable timeout are reported, not silently removed
append rejects records missing 'id' and rejects a duplicate id in the same file
Tests use tempfile directories only
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Preset files and validation
userStories.description: As a user, I can swap dimensions, weights and word tables without touching code.
acceptanceCriteria: presets/default/pad.json: five levels 1-5 per axis with zh+en anchor text; 3x3x3 word table (zh from SYSTEM_DESIGN appendix list in progress.txt, en translations); projection rule 1-2=low, 3=mid, 4-5=high
presets/default/g.json: B items B1-B4 weights .28 .18 .36 .18, E items E1-E4 weights .22 .14 .36 .28, G=(B+E)/2, 0-10 anchors 0/2/5/8/10, zh+en labels
presets/default/xp.json: six daily dimensions with caps 18,16,16,14,14,12 (sum 90), levels 0-4, ordinary outcome cap 10, event bonuses uncapped; generic zh+en descriptions; NO personal events
etrace/presets.py loads a preset by name and validates: weights in each group sum to 1.0 (+/-1e-9), word table has exactly 27 cells, caps are positive
Invalid preset raises ValueError naming the bad field
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: PAD core model
userStories.description: As the engine, I validate PAD points and summarize a day.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/pad.py: PadPoint with date, slot (early_morning|morning|noon|afternoon|evening|late_night) or exact time, P/A/D floats 0-5, provenance (self_report|model_inference), source, confidence (low|medium|high), optional duration_hours
model_inference points without a source or confidence are rejected
project(p,a,d) returns the 27-table word via preset projection
daily_summary(points) = per-axis duration-weighted mean; unknown durations use equal weight and the result is flagged estimated_duration=true
validate_day(points) fails unless morning, noon and afternoon slots are all present
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: PAD SVG chart
userStories.description: As a user, I see my day's PAD trajectory as one consistent chart.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/chart.py: pad_svg(points, kind='day'|'week') returns an SVG string
Canvas 1240x590, background #F3F5F7, y axis fixed 0-5 with ticks 1-5 labelled from preset, exactly three smooth solid lines P=#D6336C A=#F08C00 D=#1C7ED6 stroke-width 5, no dots or dashed lines
Smoothing is Gaussian-kernel local linear; bandwidth 2.5 hours for day, 0.75 days for week
Slot-only points are placed at fixed slot positions and the caption says slot positions are not exact clock times
Tests parse the SVG with xml.etree and check size, line count and colors
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: G score computation
userStories.description: As the engine, I compute B, E and G exactly from item scores.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/g.py: compute(items, preset) returns B, E, G using preset weights; no rounding before the final value; display helper rounds to 1 decimal
A group is computed only if all four items have values; G only if both B and E exist; otherwise the value is None (never 0)
Every item score carries provenance, source and confidence; items without them are rejected
legend(preset, language) returns the symbol explanation text (G=(B+E)/2, B and E formulas, item names, 0-10 anchors, 'not a clinical scale')
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: G continuity gap fill
userStories.description: As the engine, I fill missing item scores transparently.
acceptanceCriteria: g.gap_fill(history, date) fills only missing items, in fixed order: linear interpolation between nearest left/right real values (historical_bridge), else carry forward nearest earlier value (continuity_carry_forward), else 5.0 (scale_prior)
Filled items always have confidence=low, method, neighbor dates and values recorded; the day gets explicit_gap_fill=true
When a later real value appears, re-running gap_fill replaces a carry-forward with a bridge as a NEW revision; the old revision is kept
Gap-filled days are excluded by g.training_eligible(day)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Frozen predictions and calibration gate
userStories.description: As the engine, I learn from feedback without fooling myself.
acceptanceCriteria: g.predict(...) appends a prediction snapshot (id, date, revision, rubric_version, items, created_at) to predictions.jsonl; snapshots are never edited
g.feedback(...) requires a prediction_id whose created_at is earlier than the feedback time, else rejects
Only numeric targets explicitly given by the user count as training labels; text-only feedback is stored with targets={}
Numeric bias correction is enabled only after 10 training days plus 10 later test days show lower mean absolute error than no correction; otherwise g.correction_enabled() is False
Labels from a different rubric_version are not mixed into error stats
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: XP scoring
userStories.description: As a user, my daily XP reflects real growth and big moments are not flattened.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/xp.py: score_day(levels, ordinary, events, preset) where each dimension level is 0-4 and points = cap * level / 4
ordinary outcome is clamped to 0..10; events each need a unique event_id and occurred_on date; total has no daily cap and is rounded to an integer
An event_id already booked on any earlier day is rejected (single booking)
week_total(days) sums the displayed daily totals only; no weekly bonus; missing days are reported as missing, never counted as 0
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Rule store with scoped supersession
userStories.description: As the system, the newest user instruction wins within the same scope.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/rules.py: add_rule(rule_id, scope, text, expressed_at, source_feedback_id) and active_rules()
A new rule with the same scope and later expressed_at supersedes the old one; the old rule leaves the active set; different scopes coexist
expressed_at is the user's original expression time, not the file write time; an earlier-expressed rule added later does NOT supersede a newer one
Every change appends a decision record to decisions.jsonl (old, new, scope, reason)
rules.json is written atomically and records a monotonically increasing version
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Journal file format and protected blocks
userStories.description: As a user, nothing I write is ever silently changed by the AI.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/journal.py parses and writes Markdown with <!-- trace:ai:NAME --> / <!-- trace:user:NAME --> / <!-- trace:verbatim --> block markers as in docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md section 3.3

new_note(date, preset, language) creates the next-day note: empty G self-rating table (8 items), empty PAD self table (morning/noon/afternoon + other), journal zone, feedback zone; empty cells stay empty
replace_ai_block(doc, name, text) only touches ai blocks; save() compares hashes of all user and verbatim blocks before vs after and raises ProtectedBlockChanged on any difference
Round-trip test: parse then save an unmodified file is byte-identical, including Chinese text and trailing spaces
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Feedback zone ingestion
userStories.description: As a user, I give feedback by writing in my note.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/feedback.py: ingest(journal_dir) reads every user:feedback block, splits entries by blank line, stores each new entry verbatim in feedback.jsonl with id = note date + block + content hash, observed_at, and the date it refers to
Re-running ingest does not duplicate entries; an edited entry is stored as a new version linked to the previous one
Template placeholder text is never ingested as feedback
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: CLI
userStories.description: As a user or agent, I drive everything from one command.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -m etrace with subcommands: init, note new DATE, pad add FILE, pad chart DATE, g predict FILE, g feedback FILE, g report, xp score FILE, feedback ingest, rules list, validate
Commands that take FILE accept agent-produced JSON and print a validation error with field names on bad input, exit code 2
validate checks: protected block hashes, store integrity (unique ids), preset validity; exits 1 on any failure
tests/test_cli.py calls cli.main(argv) against a temp data dir
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Agent task prompts (zh/en)
userStories.description: As any coding agent, I get a short task prompt that defers rules to the engine.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/prompts/{zh,en}/ contain daily.md, g.md, calibrate.md plus a shared _principles.md (the 8 invariants from SYSTEM_DESIGN 2.2)
python3 -m etrace prompt TASK renders the prompt with values from trace.toml (data_dir, timezone, language, active rules from rules.json); no absolute paths or personal data are hard-coded
Each prompt tells the agent to output JSON for the matching CLI command and to run 'python3 -m etrace validate' at the end
Each rendered prompt is under 6000 characters (test enforces)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Scheduler adapters
userStories.description: As a user, I install the daily schedule for my agent of choice.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -m etrace schedule --target codex|claude-code|cron --out DIR writes files but never installs them
codex target writes one automation.toml per task (kind=cron, rrule from trace.toml times, prompt from US-014 render)
cron target writes a crontab snippet calling the agent CLI with the rendered prompt file; claude-code target writes a shell script using 'claude -p'
Tests check generated times match trace.toml and timezone
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Optional Notion output adapter
userStories.description: As a Notion user, I can mirror my daily report into a Notion page.
acceptanceCriteria: etrace/adapters/notion.py converts a journal file to Notion block JSON (headings, paragraphs, tables, callouts) and pushes via urllib to the Notion API using a token read from the file path in trace.toml
Local Markdown stays the source of truth; Notion push never reads back into user blocks
Tests mock the HTTP layer; no network in tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes

userStories.title: Privacy guard, example persona and README
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I am sure no personal data ships.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_privacy.py scans every tracked file for email addresses, 32-hex Notion-style IDs, '/Users/' paths and fails if any are found (allowlist only for example.com emails)
examples/ contains a fictional persona with 3 days of journal notes and expected outputs; an end-to-end test runs note -> pad add -> g predict -> xp score -> validate on it
README.md (English) and README.zh.md: what it is, the 8 principles, quickstart, 'not a clinical tool' notice
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes
